title: Breast cancer
subtitle: Every decision runs off subtype (HR+/HER2−, HER2+, TNBC) crossed with stage · AJCC 8th adds grade + ER/PR/HER2 as prognostic staging (does not apply pathologically after neoadjuvant therapy)
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Breast Cancer (Schultz C, Khan S, Sidhu K, Yang M, Dalal N, Tsai J) · NCCN 5.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Bilateral mammography + ultrasound; MRI or contrast-enhanced mammogram if indicated
Core biopsy with clip placement
Pathology: ER/PR, HER2 (IHC ± DISH — must do DISH if IHC 2+), grade, Ki-67
“High risk”: HR weak/negative, HER2+, TNBC, high grade, Ki-67 >20%, inflammatory, angiosarcoma, malignant phyllodes
Genetic testing: dx age ≤50 (NCCN) or ≤65 (ASCO), bilateral at any age, or TNBC
Stage I–IIB: no routine staging imaging — only if directed by signs, symptoms or labs
Stage III: CT chest/abdomen ± pelvis + bone scan, or PET/CT
Stage IV or recurrent: brain MRI if CNS symptoms, spine MRI if cord-compression symptoms, and biopsy the first recurrence — ideally a metastatic site

blocks.heading: Staging, margins & in-situ disease
rows: chest wall (4a) · skin edema, ulceration, satellite nodules (4b) · both (4c) · 4d = inflammatory
1–3 / 4–9 / ≥10 axillary nodes; pN1mi = >0.2–2 mm; pN0(i+) = isolated tumor cells
≥2 mm for DCIS and invasive; positive or close → discuss re-excision
prefix yc / yp; pathologic complete response = ypT0 ypN0 cM0
lumpectomy + whole-breast RT · or mastectomy ± SLN · or lumpectomy alone if small and age >70. If ER+, tamoxifen × 5 yr (NSABP B-24)
florid / pleomorphic → excise to negative margins; classical does not need negative margins

boxes: BCS if clear margins + acceptable cosmesis
mastectomy if not BCS-suitable, gene mutation,
prior mantle RT, or patient preference
omit SLNB if <2 cm, normal US, age ≥70 (SOUND)
Oncotype DX on the surgical specimen
chemo by recurrence score + menopausal status
TCHP or TCH ×6; TH ×12 wk; AC→TH(P)

blocks.heading: Neoadjuvant therapy — local-regional disease
rows: ddAC → T, or TC ×4 — the same regimens used adjuvantly
blocks.footnote: Indications: inflammatory or inoperable disease · T4 or N2–3 · TNBC or HER2+ with T2 or N1 · to downsize for breast conservation or downstage the axilla. T2/T3 meeting BCS criteria except for size → consider neoadjuvant. Response guides post-operative escalation — the main argument for treating first.

blocks.heading: † Oncotype DX — when to add chemotherapy
rows: RS 11–25 → endocrine therapy alone; chemotherapy adds nothing
RS 16–25 → consider adding chemotherapy — a real benefit in this group
blocks.footnote: Node-negative cutoffs from TAILORx (Sparano, NEJM 2018); node-positive from RxPONDER. Applies to ER/PR-positive, HER2-negative disease with up to 3 positive nodes; sent on the surgical specimen. † The handbook does not state these cutoffs — it defers to NCCN.

blocks.heading: Adjuvant escalation — HR+/HER2−
rows: 150 mg BID × 2 years with endocrine therapy — ≥4 positive nodes, OR 1–3 nodes plus grade 3, tumor ≥5 cm, or Ki-67 ≥20%
400 mg daily, 21 days on / 7 off × 3 years with endocrine therapy — any stage IIB or III, or stage IIA with grade 3 (or grade 2 with high genomic risk or Ki-67 ≥20%)
300 mg BID × 1 year — high-risk HER2-negative disease with a germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — regimens, endocrine therapy, metastatic disease and supportive care

blocks.heading: Regimens & dosing
rows: doxorubicin 60 + cyclophosphamide 600 d1 → then paclitaxel 175 (or 80). Filgrastim d3–10 or pegfilgrastim d2
AC q14d ×4; then T q14d ×4 or q7d ×12
carboplatin AUC 5 d1 + paclitaxel 80 d1, 8, 15 + pembrolizumab 200 d1 → then doxorubicin 60 + cyclophosphamide 600 d1
docetaxel 75 + carboplatin AUC 6 + trastuzumab 8→6 mg/kg (± pertuzumab 840→420) d1
paclitaxel 80 weekly ×12 + trastuzumab 4→2 mg/kg weekly, then 6 mg/kg q3wk to 1 year
AC q14d ×4 → paclitaxel 80 weekly ×12 + trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to 1 year
3.6 mg/kg IV d1 — residual disease after preoperative therapy
blocks.footnote: All doses mg/m² unless stated. Avoid concurrent trastuzumab — especially trastuzumab + pertuzumab — with an anthracycline: significant cardiotoxicity. Cardiac monitoring every 3 months on trastuzumab. If T-DM1 is stopped for toxicity, give trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to complete 1 year.

blocks.heading: Bone-directed therapy
rows: zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q4wk (may extend to q12wk after 12 months) · pamidronate 90 mg IV q3–4wk · denosumab 120 mg SQ q4wk
denosumab 60 mg SQ q6 months · zoledronic acid 5 mg IV yearly · alendronate 70 mg PO weekly · calcium 1000 mg + vitamin D 800 IU daily

blocks.heading: Surveillance
items: H&P every 6–12 months × 5 years, then annually
Annual mammogram; consider annual screening ultrasound if dense breast tissue, or CEM in lieu of mammogram + ultrasound
Annual gynecologic assessment if on tamoxifen with a uterus
Baseline DEXA before starting an aromatase inhibitor or after ovarian ablation, then every 1–2 years
Assess and actively encourage adherence to endocrine therapy
Lifestyle: alcohol <3 drinks/week, ≥150 min moderate exercise weekly, healthy BMI, Mediterranean diet
DCIS: H&P + clinical breast exam q6 months × 5 years, mammogram q12 months

blocks.heading: Adjuvant endocrine therapy
items: Premenopausal: tamoxifen 20 mg/d × 5–10 years — 5 years cuts recurrence 40% and death 30%; extending to 10 years cuts recurrence a further 25% and mortality 29%
Add ovarian suppression if high risk — goserelin 3.6 mg SQ q4wk, leuprolide 3.75 mg monthly, or oophorectomy (SOFT)
Postmenopausal: aromatase inhibitor × 5–10 years — anastrozole 1 mg, letrozole 2.5 mg (non-steroidal), exemestane 25 mg (steroidal) daily. Switch class if intolerant; tamoxifen if AI contraindicated
Tamoxifen is a CYP2D6 prodrug — avoid paroxetine and fluoxetine (also quinidine, cimetidine); citalopram and venlafaxine are acceptable. CYP2D6 genotyping is not recommended
Menopause = prior bilateral oophorectomy, age ≥60, or <60 with amenorrhea ≥12 months off chemo/tamoxifen/ovarian suppression and postmenopausal FSH + estradiol

blocks.heading: Metastatic HR+/HER2− sequencing
items: First line — de novo metastatic, or progression >12 months after endocrine therapy: aromatase inhibitor + CDK4/6 inhibitor

Progression on adjuvant ET, or relapse within 12 months of it → check NGS. PIK3CA-mutant: inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant. Wild-type: fulvestrant 500 mg IM d0, 14, 28 then q28d + a CDK4/6 inhibitor
Progression on CDK4/6i + ET → switch CDK4/6 inhibitor — ribociclib with alternative ET (MAINTAIN) or abemaciclib + fulvestrant (postMONARCH)
Endocrine-resistant: everolimus 10 mg + exemestane 25 mg daily, then chemotherapy
ADCs: T-DXd if HER2-low or ultralow · sacituzumab govitecan · datopotamab deruxtecan

blocks.heading: Surgical & radiation pearls
items: Inflammatory breast cancer: staging work-up → neoadjuvant chemotherapy → modified radical mastectomy → postoperative chest wall + regional nodal radiation — even with a pathologic complete response. Delayed reconstruction; BCS contraindicated; ALND indicated
Relative contraindications to BCS radiation: Li-Fraumeni, active connective tissue disease involving skin (scleroderma, lupus), prior chest radiation, large tumor-to-breast-volume ratio
Reconstruction with planned radiation: preferred is immediate tissue expander → expansion → radiation → exchange to implant, or delayed autologous
Nipple-sparing mastectomy: ischemia and necrosis risk with high BMI, large or ptotic breasts, prior radiation or breast surgery
Lymphedema ~5% after SLNB, highest after ALND + radiation — screen at visits; consider LYMPHA at nodal dissection; class I compression sleeve; PT referral
BIA-ALCL — associated with textured implants; very rare; diagnosed on cytology; requires complete resection of capsule, implant and any mass
